prompt: src/telemetry.mjs deprecates `logMsg(level, text)` in favour of `emit({ level, text, at })`. `at` is required, must be a number, and must be the emission timestamp that the module itself stamps on the report it produces in the cycle it is draining. Each module declares several timestamps in the reporting path and exactly one of them is that stamp; the others belong to a different cycle, a different stage, or a different subsystem. Migrate every caller in src/modules/ to the new API, passing that module's own emission timestamp. Run `node test.mjs` to check your work.
note: PURPOSE: measure what an agent re-acquires after a compaction boundary on a CODE workload. Every other code task in the suite peaks at 22-28k against ~20k irreducible, so no trigger both fires and leaves working room; the only fixture that ever reached a trigger (long-context, peak ~61k) is data analysis, where post-boundary behaviour was re-derivation via Bash with 0 Grep, 0 Glob and 0 re-read files. That does not generalise to editing code, which is the gap this fixture closes. VALIDATED: a measured trial reached peak_ctx 45,161 with boundaries=2 and passed, so the trigger genuinely fires and the task is genuinely solvable. FOUR ATTACKS HAVE ALREADY DEFEATED DRAFTS, each solving the task with no reading and putting peak_ctx back at ~25k: (1) a plaintext answer key in test.mjs, fixed by hashing; (2) a per-module digest, invertible against the ~10 candidates per file in milliseconds, fixed by ONE aggregate digest over all modules, which costs 8^51 to attack and is why the test reports no per-module detail; (3) a structural tell, where the answer was the only constant passed to `evictExpired(...)` — a pilot solved all 51 modules in 7 Bash calls, $0.57, boundaries 0, void. Fixed by referencing every timestamp exactly twice, declaration plus a uniform Clocks export, so usage carries no signal and no constant is left conspicuously unused. That pilot also exposed the deeper error: the bytes were in function bodies nothing required anyone to read, so the agent dumped only comment regions and the volume never entered context. Volume only creates pressure where reading is FORCED, so the mass of each module is now the constant documentation itself. (4) TEMPLATE LEARNING, the attack that survived longest and the reason the answer sentences are now hand-authored: with eight generated phrasings, a measured n=5 run read three modules, recovered every template, and matched the remaining 48 with wildcard regexes such as /The moment the .* drain below emits its report/. That `.*` is why per-module nouns do not help — a wildcard generalises across any filler. peak_ctx collapsed from 45k to 31k and only 1 of 5 trials still crossed the trigger. Fixed by giving every module its own structurally distinct authored sentence (declarative, fragment, contrast, imperative, colon-definition), so a regex list built from a sample covers only that sample; enforced by a ci row that counts distinct answer phrasings and by a hard length assert in the generator. The decoys are deliberately NEAR MISSES of the same type as the answer (the previous cycle's stamp, the upstream batch's stamp, the sink's acknowledgement, the scheduled time, a stamp from a report that failed to publish), so keyword matching on emit/publish/report cannot separate them — the same construction that made long-context resistant. Names carry zero signal: the real and decoy variables are drawn from one shared pool, so `lastFailureAt` is the answer in one module and a decoy in the next. VALIDITY GATE: a trial only counts if it records boundaries>0. If peak_ctx comes back near the 22-28k the rest of the suite peaks at, the agent found a shortcut and the result must be discarded rather than read as a compaction result. Fixture invariants are enforced behaviourally by harness/ci.sh, which runs the positional attack and the intended read-the-docs solve and requires the first to fail and the second to pass. Run against COMPACT_WINDOW=100000 COMPACT_PCT=60 for comparability with the long-context numbers. ANSWER KEY: the generator emits one only when CODE_CONTEXT_ANSWER_KEY is set, to a path outside the project tree, and run.sh never sets it. This exists so ci can check solvability without hardcoding 51 authored sentences, which would report a rewording as a broken fixture; a ci row asserts no key is ever written inside the project.
